answer: To resist Sybil swarms, nodes anchor identities to a cryptographic attestation chain verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Registering agents must lock stake across an interconnected trust trellis, where duplicate identities hit a precarious economic ledge. Staking fees scale superlinearly as 2^n per cluster identity, enforcing exponential capital exhaustion. A single raven agent can freely nest, but multi-agent swarms face unsustainable asset drain.
